cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
Only Dutch municipalities with an eligible 220/380 kV project may apply; there is no consortium.
- Lead applicant: the municipality where the substation or line is built. Where a line crosses several municipalities, each applies for its own kilometres.
- Partners: none are required. The municipality must organise a participation process that invites at least all residents within 200 metres of the project.
- Distribution of work: the municipality chooses and carries out the investments; contractors or local organisations may build them, but the municipality must avoid unlawful state aid to companies that build the facilities.
- Suits best: municipalities, and through them local organisations, community groups and contractors who carry out the quality-of-life projects.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Nothing is demonstrated: the investments are realised in the area around the high-voltage project and must follow from the participation process.
The municipality must take residents' input as the starting point, record its choices in a spending plan approved by the municipal council, and explain to participants where it departs from their wishes. This participation is separate from the participation on the spatial integration of the grid project itself, and the scheme's money may not replace measures the grid project's developer must already take under planning law.
cards.sources: Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 9; Artikel 10 Raadsbesluit; Artikel 11 Bestedingsplan; Toelichting § 4 Inzet middelen (Wettelijke ruimtelijke inpassing initiatiefnemer); § 5 Participatieproces

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer:
The scheme is paid out around TenneT's own onshore 220/380 kV grid extensions and aims to keep local support, which could reduce resistance and delays to them.
Our judgement: the list of eligible projects, including stations such as Almere, Lelystad, Wijchen and Port of Moerdijk and lines such as Diemen-Lelystad-Ens and Vierverlaten-Ens, is based on TenneT's Investment Plan 2026, and the explanatory notes state that local resistance currently delays these projects and that residents' wishes often go beyond what TenneT is legally allowed to do. TenneT's project teams could point municipalities to the scheme early, align the timing of their project decisions with it, and coordinate their own spatial-integration measures with the municipality's spending plan, since those measures cannot be funded from the grant. TenneT cannot take part itself: only municipalities may apply, and the regulation gives the grid operator no role in the application, the participation process or the spending plan.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 3; Artikel 6; Toelichting § 2 Achtergrond; § 3 Projectenlijst; § 4 Inzet middelen; Bijlage I Projectenlijst

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
A fixed amount per eligible project, from a total budget of about EUR 193.4 million, allocated first come, first served.
- Total project size: not set; the grant is a fixed amount, not a share of costs.
- Grant request: EUR 6 million per new substation, EUR 3 million per substation extension, EUR 150,000 per kilometre of new overhead line (at least 1 kilometre in the municipality, rounded to one decimal), per municipality and per physical project; a line can be combined with a substation in one application.
- Funding form: a fixed grant including VAT, paid to the municipality. The cabinet made EUR 197 million available, of which EUR 193.4 million is for the grants (including EUR 19.34 million paid into the VAT compensation fund) and about EUR 3.6 million covers RVO's costs.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 5 Hoogte, plafond en verdeling; Artikel 6, tweede lid; Toelichting § 3 Berekening; Budget
Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV (RVO page) · Budget en aanvraagperiode; Hoe hoog is de specifieke uitkering?

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The grant is a fixed amount that does not depend on costs, and the municipality need not co-finance.
- Co-financing conditions: none stated; VAT the municipality can recover through the VAT compensation fund or deduct is not covered by the grant.
cards.sources: Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 5; Artikel 7, tweede lid; Toelichting § 3 Berekening

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Only reasonable costs directly linked to improving residents' quality of life count, excluding recoverable VAT and measures the grid project must take anyway.
- Eligible costs: reasonable costs directly connected with the quality-of-life investments, made from 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2036; part of the first advance may also pay for preparation, including the participation process.
- Excluded costs: VAT the municipality can recover; landscape and spatial-integration measures the developer of the grid project is already legally required to take.
- Overheads and VAT: the grant includes VAT, but VAT is paid into the VAT compensation fund and not to the municipality.
cards.sources: Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 7 In aanmerking komende kosten; Toelichting § 3 Berekening; Uitbetaling; § 4 Inzet middelen

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: the municipality applies online to RVO with eHerkenning level 3, from 15 October 2026, 09:00, to 31 March 2031, 17:00.
- Stage 1 — Application: by 31 March 2031, 17:00, first come, first served; with a reference to the project decision, the amount and its calculation, and a participation plan.
- Additional procedure: within two years of the grant decision, the municipality sends the council decision with the spending plan, the participation report and the minutes of the council meeting.
The project decision need not be final at the time of application.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 6 Aanvraag; Artikel 10 Raadsbesluit; Toelichting § 3 Reikwijdte regeling
Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV (RVO page) · Uw aanvraag voorbereiden; Aanvragen

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
Investments must be realised within about five years of the grant, and costs count from 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2036.
- Maximum duration: two years to adopt the council decision, then three years to carry out the investments.
- Eligible-cost period: 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2036.
- Completion deadline: within three years of the council decision; in exceptional cases, for example when the investment can only start during or after construction of the grid project, the municipality may ask for an extension.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 7, eerste lid; Artikel 10, eerste lid; Artikel 12, eerste en tweede lid; Toelichting § 3 Uitbetaling; § 7 Inrichting proces
Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV (RVO page) · Na uw aanvraag

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
RVO decides within 8 weeks of a complete application, extendable once by 8 weeks.
- Funding decision: within 8 weeks, or at most 16 weeks.
- Grant agreement: none; the first advance of 20% (excluding VAT) is paid within two weeks of the decision, and the second advance of 80% within eight weeks of receiving the council decision and its annexes.
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The application must include the municipality's details, a reference to the project decision, the calculated amount and a participation plan.
- Application form: online through RVO with eHerkenning level 3 and authorisation for RVO services at eH3.
- Mandatory annexes: a participation plan describing the groups of residents and stakeholders, how they are informed and can give input, how their input is processed and fed back, and a timeline (RVO will publish a format).
- Registration: Chamber of Commerce number and bank details of the municipality.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 6, derde lid; Artikel 9, eerste lid
Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV (RVO page) · Uw aanvraag voorbereiden

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer: Applications are not scored: complete applications are granted in order of receipt while budget lasts, and rejected only if the municipality is unlikely to meet its obligations.
cards.sources: Staatscourant 2026, 26122 (Regeling gebiedsinvesteringen hoogspanning op land 220/380 kV) · Artikel 5, tweede lid; Artikel 13 Afwijsgronden

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Conditions apply when the project decision falls away or the work slips.
- Conditional — project decision annulled after payment: the grant is settled at the amount actually spent on participation activities and the rest must be repaid.
- Conditional — investments cannot be completed in time: the municipality must report this to RVO at once (at least four months before the deadline) and may ask for an extension.
- Exception — a substation and a line decided at different times: only one grant per physical project; the municipality should invite stakeholders of the later decision to the first participation process or wait for the last decision.
- Recommended: RVO's expert pool for energy infrastructure projects can help set up the participation process, and a communication toolkit is available.
cards.sources:
